subject.title: Feature Request: Add .gitignore-like exclude patterns to backup CLI

question: Should OpenClaw add native backup exclude-pattern controls now, and which defaults, protected paths, and ignore-file behavior should become part of the core CLI contract?
rationale: The missing capability is clear from source, but defaults and protected recovery paths decide the balance between backup size, sensitive-file avoidance, and restorable archives.

options.title: Review the linked PR as canonical
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 to settle defaults, protected paths, manifest/JSON compatibility, proof, and security posture before landing or narrowing it.

options.title: Ship only explicit custom excludes first
options.body: Accept `--exclude` and `--exclude-file` while deferring smart defaults and auto-detected ignore files until restore completeness and sensitive-file behavior are clearer.

options.title: Decline native excludes for now
options.body: Keep core backups coarse, document current scope, and direct optional backup strategies to plugin or ClawHub paths after an explicit maintainer decision.

recommendation.title: Review the linked PR as canonical
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 to settle defaults, protected paths, manifest/JSON compatibility, proof, and security posture before landing or narrowing it.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the original backup CLI contract and are the strongest history signal for a core backup CLI product decision.
